lectures.title: It works. So why is anyone still saying no?
The patients you never meet: opportunity cost as the hidden loser
Where did this whole enterprise come from?
Norway's priority-setting system, criterion by criterion
Whose costs count? The perspective question decides the answer
What is a QALY really claiming about you?
How can you possibly measure how bad an illness feels? A map of the methods
Time trade-off and standard gamble: whose values, and what lies below zero?
Severity: absolute shortfall, proportional shortfall, or something else?
What counts as a cost, and why does the future cost less?
CEA, CUA, CBA - and why cost-of-illness answers a different question entirely
What is a life worth in money, and who decided that?
Why model at all - and which model shape fits which problem?
Building a Markov model: states, cycles, transitions and the long tail
The ICER, the plane, and why net benefit is easier to think with
Where does the threshold come from - willingness to pay, or what we displace?
Which uncertainties can more money actually fix?
Showing what you don't know: from tornado diagrams to acceptability curves
If we are unsure, should we decide now or pay to learn?
Is the QALY fair - and should the number decide?

quiz.question: A cancer drug adds half a QALY for 600 000 kr more. The line is 825 000 kr per QALY. Where does it sit?
Moving to the societal ledger, what happened to ΔE, the QALYs gained?
Why doesn't the societal saving relieve the hospital's budget?
choices: It lands in other budgets: NAV, the municipality, the family
It arrives only after the patent expires

quiz.question: Adding the return to work changed which part of the ICER?
Two patients, same operation, same half QALY. Why does only the younger one pass?
What actually differs between those two points?
Where do productivity gains belong in a Norwegian submission?
choices: In a sensitivity analysis beside it

quiz.question: Under a narrow hospital-budget perspective, who absorbs the costs that disappear from the sum?
The next respondent is indifferent at 8 years instead of 6. What is u?
If respondents discount distant years, what does the raw ratio x over t do to the utility?
Using public values rather than patient values, a treatment that only adds years in that state looks…
So why do the guidelines use general-population values?
choices: The public judge health states more accurately
The public fund the system and bear the risk

quiz.question: Raising the birds at risk a hundredfold changed stated willingness to pay by how much?
Compared with real payments, hypothetical answers are usually:
Which of these does a cost-utility analysis, by construction, leave out?
choices: A diagnosis that changes no treatment
A drop in quality of life

quiz.question: What does the steepness of the arrow from the origin to a point measure?
Which point lies above the threshold line?
Which cases can be decided without naming any threshold?
A disinvestment sits below the threshold line in the south-west. What does that mean?
choices: It releases more money than the lost health is worth
It saves money and adds health

quiz.question: An ICER of −400 000 kr per QALY — which quadrant is that technology in?
choices: Either one — the sign can't tell you

quiz.question: A point sitting ABOVE the threshold line has:
So what does net benefit still require of you?
choices: A value of λ, committed to before you look at the data

quiz.question: What does this table tell you about how likely each corner is?
choices: The base case is most likely

quiz.question: Why is the worst-case corner the least trustworthy number in the table?
choices: It needs both parameters extreme at the same time

quiz.question: Which bar tells you most about where extra research money should go?
What can a tornado diagram NOT tell you?
choices: Which parameter swings the result most

quiz.question: The curve reads about 0.7 at lambda = 825,000 kr per QALY. What does that mean?
choices: In 70% of the draws the drug had the higher net benefit

quiz.question: The manufacturer halves the price. What happens to nusinersen's curve?
choices: It slides left, reaching high probability at a lower lambda
It stays put but gets steeper

quiz.question: What does the widest bar of a tornado diagram tell you?
choices: The result is most sensitive to that parameter
The probability the drug is cost-effective

quiz.question: A CEAC reads 0.7 at the severity-weighted λ. That means:
choices: 70% of the simulated draws favour the new drug at that λ
We are 70% sure the model is correct
